evidence: The gate password is written in plain text in a comment next to its hash, in a public GitHub repo. It is one dictionary word, so the hash is also trivially reversible.
proposed_fix: Owner picks a new long passphrase; store only the hash; delete the comment. Old password stays in git history, so treat it as burned.
risk: Low. Only the hash value changes; password_id keys stay.

evidence: Gated pages ship their full content in the HTML as base64. Decoded without the password: /alltech/database/guides/me75-full-flash-bdm/ (313 words), /alltech/database/guides/bosch-me75-manual/ (33 words). The gate only hides, it does not protect.
proposed_fix: Decide per page: make it public, remove it from the site, or move it behind real access control (for example Vercel password protection or a separate private site). A static site cannot keep a secret in its own HTML.
risk: Medium. Changes who can read paid or private guides; needs owner decision.
